## CWE rule
CWE-120 — Buffer Copy without Checking Size of Input (Classic Buffer Overflow)
Description: Data is copied into a fixed-size buffer without checking that the input length fits in the destination buffer. Out-of-bounds reads and writes (CWE-125/787) caused by unvalidated indexes or lengths also fall under this entry.
Vulnerability indicators:
- strcpy/strcat/sprintf/gets on fixed-size buffers with a source of unchecked length
- memcpy/memmove with a length derived from external input and no comparison against the destination capacity
- Length computations that can underflow or overflow before the copy
- Index or offset derived from external input used to access an array or buffer without bounds checking
Safe patterns:
- Explicit len <= sizeof(dst) check (or allocated capacity) before the copy
- snprintf/strlcpy with the correct destination size and truncation handling

## CWE rule
CWE-120 — Buffer Copy without Checking Size of Input (Classic Buffer Overflow)
Description: Data is copied into a fixed-size buffer without checking that the input length fits in the destination buffer. Out-of-bounds reads and writes (CWE-125/787) caused by unvalidated indexes or lengths also fall under this entry.
Vulnerability indicators:
- strcpy/strcat/sprintf/gets on fixed-size buffers with a source of unchecked length
- memcpy/memmove with a length derived from external input and no comparison against the destination capacity

- Index or offset derived from external input used to access an array or buffer without bounds checking
Safe patterns:
- Explicit len <= sizeof(dst) check (or allocated capacity) before the copy
- snprintf/strlcpy with the correct destination size and truncation handling

Description: Data is copied into a fixed-size buffer without checking that the input length fits in the destination buffer. Out-of-bounds reads and writes (CWE-125/787) caused by unvalidated indexes or lengths also fall under this entry.
Vulnerability indicators:
- strcpy/strcat/sprintf/gets on fixed-size buffers with a source of unchecked length
- memcpy/memmove with a length derived from external input and no comparison against the destination capacity
- Length computations that can underflow or overflow before the copy
- Index or offset derived from external input used to access an array or buffer without bounds checking
Safe patterns:
- Explicit len <= sizeof(dst) check (or allocated capacity) before the copy
- snprintf/strlcpy with the correct destination size and truncation handling

CWE-120 — Buffer Copy without Checking Size of Input (Classic Buffer Overflow)

- strcpy/strcat/sprintf/gets on fixed-size buffers with a source of unchecked length

- Index or offset derived from external input used to access an array or buffer without bounds checking
Safe patterns:
- Explicit len <= sizeof(dst) check (or allocated capacity) before the copy
- snprintf/strlcpy with the correct destination size and truncation handling

- Explicit len <= sizeof(dst) check (or allocated capacity) before the copy

## CWE rule
CWE-120 — Buffer Copy without Checking Size of Input (Classic Buffer Overflow)
Description: Data is copied into a fixed-size buffer without checking that the input length fits in the destination buffer. Out-of-bounds reads and writes (CWE-125/787) caused by unvalidated indexes or lengths also fall under this entry.
Vulnerability indicators:
- strcpy/strcat/sprintf/gets on fixed-size buffers with a source of unchecked length
- memcpy/memmove with a length derived from external input and no comparison against the destination capacity
- Length computations that can underflow or overflow before the copy
- Index or offset derived from external input used to access an array or buffer without bounds checking
Safe patterns:
- Explicit len <= sizeof(dst) check (or allocated capacity) before the copy
- snprintf/strlcpy with the correct destination size and truncation handling

CWE-120 — Buffer Copy without Checking Size of Input (Classic Buffer Overflow)
Description: Data is copied into a fixed-size buffer without checking that the input length fits in the destination buffer. Out-of-bounds reads and writes (CWE-125/787) caused by unvalidated indexes or lengths also fall under this entry.
Vulnerability indicators:
- strcpy/strcat/sprintf/gets on fixed-size buffers with a source of unchecked length
- memcpy/memmove with a length derived from external input and no comparison against the destination capacity
- Length computations that can underflow or overflow before the copy
- Index or offset derived from external input used to access an array or buffer without bounds checking
Safe patterns:
- Explicit len <= sizeof(dst) check (or allocated capacity) before the copy
- snprintf/strlcpy with the correct destination size and truncation handling

- Explicit len <= sizeof(dst) check (or allocated capacity) before the copy
- snprintf/strlcpy with the correct destination size and truncation handling

## CWE rule
CWE-120 — Buffer Copy without Checking Size of Input (Classic Buffer Overflow)
Description: Data is copied into a fixed-size buffer without checking that the input length fits in the destination buffer. Out-of-bounds reads and writes (CWE-125/787) caused by unvalidated indexes or lengths also fall under this entry.
Vulnerability indicators:
- strcpy/strcat/sprintf/gets on fixed-size buffers with a source of unchecked length
- memcpy/memmove with a length derived from external input and no comparison against the destination capacity
- Length computations that can underflow or overflow before the copy
- Index or offset derived from external input used to access an array or buffer without bounds checking
Safe patterns:
- Explicit len <= sizeof(dst) check (or allocated capacity) before the copy
- snprintf/strlcpy with the correct destination size and truncation handling

## CWE rule
CWE-120 — Buffer Copy without Checking Size of Input (Classic Buffer Overflow)
Description: Data is copied into a fixed-size buffer without checking that the input length fits in the destination buffer. Out-of-bounds reads and writes (CWE-125/787) caused by unvalidated indexes or lengths also fall under this entry.
Vulnerability indicators:
- strcpy/strcat/sprintf/gets on fixed-size buffers with a source of unchecked length
- memcpy/memmove with a length derived from external input and no comparison against the destination capacity
- Length computations that can underflow or overflow before the copy
- Index or offset derived from external input used to access an array or buffer without bounds checking
Safe patterns:
- Explicit len <= sizeof(dst) check (or allocated capacity) before the copy
- snprintf/strlcpy with the correct destination size and truncation handling

- Explicit len <= sizeof(dst) check (or allocated capacity) before the copy
- snprintf/strlcpy with the correct destination size and truncation handling

CWE-120 — Buffer Copy without Checking Size of Input (Classic Buffer Overflow)

- strcpy/strcat/sprintf/gets on fixed-size buffers with a source of unchecked length

- Index or offset derived from external input used to access an array or buffer without bounds checking
Safe patterns:
- Explicit len <= sizeof(dst) check (or allocated capacity) before the copy
- snprintf/strlcpy with the correct destination size and truncation handling
